title: Perform a server script and return JSON
purpose: Call an explicitly resolved server script with a versioned JSON request, wait for completion, and separate call failure from the server script's JSON business result.
preconditions: The target file is hosted and Perform Script on Server is configured for Wait for completion On.
The server script name is resolved from target-solution metadata and the caller has permission to invoke it.
The server script implements the json-parameter-validation pattern before business work.
The server script uses {{SERVER_CONTEXT_PLAN}} to rebuild every required layout, found set, and current record in its independent FMSE session.
Related-file authentication and the handling of retries or duplicate requests are explicitly designed.

steps.name: Set Error Capture
steps.purpose: Keep caller-side invocation errors and server-side validation errors under explicit script control.

partialConditions.psos: FMSE always behaves as Set Error Capture On; do not depend on an Off state.

steps.name: Set Variable
steps.purpose: Store the request JSON, call error, raw script result, and parsed result in local variables.

steps.name: Perform Script on Server
steps.purpose: Invoke {{SERVER_SCRIPT_NAME}} with Wait for completion On and the explicit JSON request.

steps.name: If
steps.purpose: Branch first on caller-side invocation error and then on the server JSON result.

steps.name: Else
steps.purpose: Keep transport/session failures separate from server business failures.

steps.name: End If
steps.purpose: Close call and business-result branches explicitly.

steps.name: Exit Script
steps.purpose: Return the common JSON result from the server and, if this wrapper is itself called, from the caller.

happyPath: Build JSON containing schemaVersion {{REQUEST_SCHEMA_VERSION}}, requestId from {{REQUEST_ID_EXPRESSION}}, operation {{OPERATION_NAME}}, and payload from {{PAYLOAD_EXPRESSION}}.
Invoke {{SERVER_SCRIPT_NAME}} with Wait for completion On.
Immediately store Get ( LastError ) as the call-level result, then store Get ( ScriptResult ) separately.

In the independent FMSE session, validate Get ( ScriptParameter ) again, do not use caller variables or global-field values, and execute {{SERVER_CONTEXT_PLAN}} to rebuild layout, found set, and current record.
Have the server script return the common JSON envelope with Exit Script.
On the caller, reject a nonzero call error before interpreting the business result.
Validate and parse the returned JSON, then propagate its OK or business-error envelope without relabeling it as a call failure.

errorBranches.trigger: Perform Script on Server returns a nonzero caller-side error not classified more specifically by the resolved deployment.
errorBranches.action: Return the preserved call error and do not manufacture a server business result.

errorBranches.trigger: The resolved deployment reports that the synchronous server call did not finish within its allowed time.
errorBranches.action: Treat completion as unknown and use requestId/idempotency before any retry.

errorBranches.trigger: An administrator or server shutdown stops the FMSE session.
errorBranches.action: Treat business completion as unknown and reconcile by requestId.

errorBranches.trigger: The deployment cannot start another server session because capacity is unavailable.
errorBranches.action: Return a retryable infrastructure result only under a bounded retry policy.

errorBranches.trigger: The call succeeds but Get ( ScriptResult ) is empty, malformed JSON, or not the common result contract.
errorBranches.action: Return a contract error and preserve the raw result only in access-controlled diagnostics.

errorBranches.trigger: The server-side idempotency rule determines that requestId was already processed.
errorBranches.action: Return the prior logical outcome or the approved duplicate conflict.

errorBranches.trigger: The call succeeds and the server returns a valid envelope with ok false.
errorBranches.action: Preserve the server code/message as a business result; do not relabel it as a PSOS call failure.

concurrencyNotes: Perform Script on Server creates an independent FMSE session and does not inherit layout, found set, current record, sort order, variables, or global-field values.
Timeout or interruption can leave completion unknown; requestId and an approved idempotency design are required before retrying a write.
Concurrent or nested PSOS calls consume independent sessions and must respect deployment capacity.
Wait for completion Off is outside the completed pattern because the initiating script cannot depend on a result handoff.
securityNotes: Do not send credentials or unnecessary sensitive data in the script parameter.
Redact values for {{SENSITIVE_JSON_KEYS}} in caller and server logs.
Resolve {{RELATED_FILE_AUTHENTICATION_PLAN}} explicitly; a client-authenticated related file must not be assumed available to FMSE.
Log only approved metadata such as requestId, operation, result code, and non-sensitive diagnostic context.
Verify that the calling account may run {{SERVER_SCRIPT_NAME}} and access every object in {{SERVER_CONTEXT_PLAN}}.
